findings.title: A verifier result with no labelled outcome is still published as exercised when a bare fallback-declared headline is followed by a bold or code-quoted exercised, so the board can claim verification that never ran

evidence.value: for tier in VERIFIER_TIERS: found = {...}; if found: return fallback-declared if it is in found, else exercised. The fallback preference applies only within one tier, so a tier-2 (bold/code/Verdict) exercised returns before the tier-3 bare fallback-declared is considered.

verdict_of(text, ver): [fallback-declared (headless run infeasible; `exercised` needs a browser)] -> exercised; [fallback-declared: the flow could only be `exercised` in a browser] -> exercised; [fallback-declared. **Exercised** requires Playwright, which I lack.] -> exercised. With the JSON outcome key present, every case reads correctly.

classify() reads the full task-notification result (export_sessions.py:296,305; the result tag at :544). A contract-conformant verifier always emits report.outcome (verifier.md:57-63), which tier 1 reads first, so only a result without the JSON outcome reaches this path.

The tier order is the one the round-1 remediation for CR-PBI001-01 prescribed (labelled, then bold/code/Verdict, then bare); the writer implemented it faithfully. The defect is in that ordering, not the implementation.

findings.impact: FR-84 publishes the verifier word so the owner knows whether a change was really exercised; a false exercised is the worst failure the verifier contract names. The case needs a result without its mandated JSON block (truncated, abbreviated or non-conformant), so it is narrower than CR-PBI001-01. When it happens, though, it produces the same false claim.
findings.remediation: Keep tier 1 (the outcome key or Outcome: label) authoritative. Below it, let any un-negated fallback-declared in tiers 2 and 3 win over exercised, whatever tier each word came from: the risk is one-sided, and under-claiming is the safe direction. Add the three probe strings as VerdictOf tests.

findings.title: On Windows a runs.manual id still escapes out/runs or crashes the export: a drive-qualified id such as d:notes is written to another drive, forbidden characters raise a traceback, and a leading-dot id is written but never pushed

subject.name: RUN_ID and its use in manual(); written at exporters/export_sessions.py:841

evidence.value: RUN_ID (a copy of local _SEGMENT) refuses only a slash or backslash, C0/C1 control characters, empty, a single dot and two dots. export_sessions.py:841 writes os.path.join(out, runs, id + .json) after :823-825 have already emptied out/sessions, out/runs and out/projects.

board_config.manual accepts id d:notes; ntpath.join(worktree/out/runs, d:notes.json) gives d:notes.json, drive-relative on D:, which exists on this machine (C:, D:, E: and F: are present). An a:b write in scratch targeted A:/.b.json.TMP.tmp, outside the runs folder.

Accepted by manual(), then write_json raises OSError [Errno 22] for a?b, a*b, a|b, a-less-than-b and an id holding a double quote. The id .x writes .x.json, which the *.json glob that refresh.py uses never picks up, so the row silently never reaches the board.
CLAUDE.md:56 says the id must be one safe path segment because it becomes a file name under out/runs/. That is true on POSIX but not on win32, the platform the refresher runs on.

findings.impact: Round 2 closed what round 1 named (../x, a/b, a backslash b, ., .., empty, controls) and pins it with tests and an ast drift guard, so CR-PBI001-02 is partially resolved. The file-name escape class remains on the actual platform. A drive-qualified id writes (and os.replace can overwrite) a JSON file in the current directory of another drive. Forbidden characters abort the export with a traceback after out/ has been emptied, which refresh.py treats as a failed export, so nothing is pushed. A leading-dot id vanishes silently (writer-disclosed gap 1). The rows come from trusted, hand-written config, and the real ids (orch-adrs-spec, orch-toolchain) are safe, hence MEDIUM, as in round 1.
findings.remediation: Keep RUN_ID equal to local _SEGMENT so the drift test stays meaningful, and add an exporter-only file-name check in manual(): for example also require board_config.ID, or refuse a colon, the Windows-forbidden characters (asterisk, question mark, less-than, greater-than, pipe, double quote), a leading dot, a trailing dot or space, and the Windows device names. The exporter set only has to be a subset of the local form, and a stricter exporter keeps every exported id valid for local to_row. So the concern in change-report-r2 that tightening would diverge from the local form does not apply, and nothing under local/** needs to change. Add ManualRows cases for d:x, a?b, .x and CON, and correct CLAUDE.md:56.

findings.title: The new promise that nothing written under a Later idea is lost is untrue for text after a blank line, which is still dropped without a warning

subject.name: later_items() docstring and blank-line reset; mirrored at CLAUDE.md:32

evidence.value: if not line.strip() or RULE.match(text): current = None  (a blank line ends the idea, so a following indented nested item or paragraph has no idea to join)

Lines [- **A**: one] [    - nested] [] [    - after blank] [] [    more under A after a blank] [- **B**: two] give A: one - nested and B: two in both the worktree and origin/main; the two lines after the blanks disappear.

findings.impact: The behaviour predates this change and neither real spec has such text today, but the round-2 docstring and CLAUDE.md now state the opposite. A spec author who writes a loose nested list (common Markdown style) loses the text silently, which is what CR-PBI001-03 set out to stop.
findings.remediation: Either keep an indented line after a blank line inside the current idea (reset only on a blank line followed by an unindented non-marker line or a new top-level marker), or narrow the wording in the docstring and CLAUDE.md to up to the next blank line. Pin the choice with a FutureIterations case.
